categories.title: Vedic Literature
categories.description: Browse by Vedic corpus while keeping Samhita hymns distinct from Brahmana, Aranyaka and Upanishad texts.

collections.title: Rigveda Samhita
collections.description: A story drawn directly from a Rigveda Samhita hymn.
collections.note: Rigveda 1.32 is presented on its own terms. Later Puranic Vritra narratives are not merged into it.

collections.title: Samaveda and associated literature
collections.description: Available readers come from the Kena and Chandogya Upanishads associated with Samaveda literature.
collections.note: These are Upanishadic passages, not passages from the Samaveda Samhita.

collections.title: Shukla Yajurveda and associated literature
collections.description: The available reader comes from the Brihadaranyaka Upanishad in the Vajasaneyi tradition.
collections.note: The source remains the Brihadaranyaka Upanishad; association does not make it a Yajurveda Samhita passage.

collections.title: Krishna Yajurveda and associated literature
collections.description: The available reader comes from the Katha Upanishad associated with the Katha school of the Krishna Yajurveda.
collections.note: The source remains the Katha Upanishad; it is not described as a direct passage from the Yajurveda Samhita.

collections.title: Atharvaveda and associated literature
collections.description: Reserved for future readers with verified Atharvavedic sources.
collections.note: No current story is assigned without an exact verified source.

categories.title: Puranic Literature
categories.description: Collections follow the text named by each reader. Parallel accounts remain labelled as parallel accounts.

collections.title: Shiva Purana
collections.description: Readers whose primary source is the Shiva Purana, plus one clearly labelled devotional synthesis with a related Shiva Purana passage.
collections.note: A deity’s presence alone never determines this classification.

collections.title: Srimad Bhagavata Purana
collections.description: Readers grounded in named skandhas and chapters of the Srimad Bhagavata Purana.
collections.note: Where another Purana has a distinct telling, the card and source notes preserve that distinction.

collections.title: Vishnu Purana
collections.description: Readers directly supported by a named Vishnu Purana passage.
collections.note: The collection is based on source references, not on whether Vishnu appears in a story.

collections.title: Linga Purana
collections.description: Reserved for future readers with verified Linga Purana passages.
collections.note: The Infinite Shiva Linga reader is not placed here because its current primary source is the Shiva Purana.

collections.title: Skanda Purana
collections.description: Readers with verified Skanda Purana parallels or related passages.
collections.note: These cards state when the canonical reader follows another text or a wider devotional tradition.

collections.title: Brahmanda Purana
collections.description: The Lalita Mahatmya reader within the Brahmanda Purana.
collections.note: The page follows its own Shakta textual setting.

collections.title: Markandeya Purana
collections.description: Readers from the Devi Mahatmya embedded within the Markandeya Purana.
collections.note: Devi Mahatmya is identified as a text within this Purana, not as a separate Purana.

collections.title: Matsya Purana
collections.description: A reader directly supported by the Matsya Purana.
collections.note: Other flood narratives are not merged into this account.

categories.title: Epics
categories.description: Episodes remain attached to their named epic and textual location.

collections.title: Valmiki Ramayana
collections.description: Readers grounded in named kandas and passages of the Valmiki Ramayana.
collections.note: Later retellings and Puranic parallels are not silently inserted.

collections.title: Mahabharata
collections.description: The Savitri–Satyavan account in the Vana Parva, following chapters 293–299 in the owner-supplied Gita Press Sanskrit–Hindi edition.
collections.note: This epic's verified narrative is kept distinct from Puranic parallels and later Savitri observance traditions.

categories.title: Other Texts and Traditions
categories.description: Exact texts and wider traditions that need their own context rather than being flattened into a parent label.

collections.title: Devi Mahatmya
collections.description: The Devi Mahatmya stories currently available in the library.
collections.note: Devi Mahatmya is a text within the Markandeya Purana. Both classifications lead to the same canonical story pages.

collections.title: Relevant Upanishads
collections.description: Readers from the Katha, Kena, Brihadaranyaka and Chandogya Upanishads.
collections.note: Each card names its exact Upanishad. Vedic association is additional context, never a replacement source.

collections.title: Kalasamhara devotional tradition
collections.description: A reader whose familiar narrative is presented as a devotional tradition alongside related but distinct Puranic passages.
collections.note: It is not labelled as a literal translation of one Skanda Purana or Shiva Purana chapter.
